headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise if MinerU ingests shared content from the unverified awesome-nlp list; no direct evidence of a blocked pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can ingest files and exposes an MCP server, so if awesome-nlp content is copied into a shared workspace or passed through a shared channel, prompt-like text could influence downstream parsing. awesome-nlp itself is a static list and not runnable, so the interaction is indirect, but the shared-content pathway is plausible enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp content is copied into a file or message that MinerU parses as input, injection risk exists.
IF MinerU is connected through MCP to a workflow that trusts extracted text as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp content out of MinerU input paths.
Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted text as instructions.
Use a separate workspace for list curation and document processing.
Add a manual review step before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for extracted text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no egress, while MinerU is documented as private/offline but also lists REST/FastAPI/MCP surfaces and allowlisted egress. With no shared workspace or sensitive data class shown, leakage is possible only through unusual integration, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are routed from a shared workspace into MinerU, extracted text may leave the local boundary through its API surfaces.
IF MinerU is configured to call allowlisted external services, document contents can be exposed beyond awesome-nlp's static list context.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in the shared input directory.
Run MinerU with external API calls disabled.
Use separate accounts or workspaces for the two agents.
Review allowlist entries before processing documents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities, while MinerU cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write surface in the profiles, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, this assessment would change.
IF awesome-nlp is wrapped in a custom runtime with write privileges, conflict risk could emerge.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp non-runnable.
Do not grant shared write access to MinerU.
Use read-only mounts for any shared inputs.
Separate git worktrees if either agent is later made writable.
requires-engineering: add lock coordination for mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU can consume files and emit structured extraction through API/MCP surfaces, so if awesome-nlp-derived content is treated as authoritative input, downstream automation could propagate errors. awesome-nlp itself is only a reference list, so the cascade is indirect, but the lack of verification in the pair makes medium the safer choice.
conditions: IF MinerU output is used as authoritative data without human verification, extraction errors can cascade.
IF awesome-nlp entries are copied into a document pipeline, any malformed text can be propagated by MinerU.
mitigations: Require human review of MinerU outputs before action.
Treat awesome-nlp as reference material only.
Add schema validation to extracted fields.
Log source-to-output mappings for review.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. awesome-nlp touches no data classes, and MinerU's profile does not show regulated-data handling or conflicting compliance obligations, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into MinerU, a separate compliance review is required.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdiction-specific policy not shown here, reassess compliance.
mitigations: Avoid processing regulated data until policies are confirmed.
Document retention settings before deployment.
Confirm residency requirements for any hosted API use.
Review access logs after initial runs.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
